The evaluation worker scores each rollout with `runner.rollout_score(result)`. That scoring treats a rollout as failed only when it has no reward and has an error. A verifier that wrote a reward with no answered model call therefore still counts as scored. The training path, `reef/train/task_rollouts.py`, shares the same `rollout_score`, so the check belongs in the evaluation worker. That leaves training rollouts unchanged. `reef/harness/tasks/rollouts.py` is the second candidate, in case the change goes into the shared `TaskRollout` or `rollout_score`.

The change belongs in `RecordRules` in `reef/storage/item_kinds.py`. That class inherits `stored_digest` and `matches_stored` from `JsonItemRules`, and both compute `json_digest(content)` over the whole content, including `created_at`.

- **`stored_digest`:** `RecordRules` needs an override that drops `created_at` before hashing.
- **`matches_stored`:** it needs an override that hashes stored content without `created_at` and compares that with the new digest. A record stored before this change has `created_at` in its digest, so this is how a retry with a different time still matches.

I didn't read `reef/storage/data.py`, which also references `matches_stored`. It most likely only calls the method, so I've listed it as a lower-probability candidate.

Changes go in `reef/storage/item_kinds.py`: `RecordRules` needs its own `stored_digest` that leaves out `created_at`, and its own `matches_stored` that accepts the older digest. I did not edit any file.

- **Digest:** `JsonItemRules.stored_digest` (line 147) returns `json_digest(content)`. `RecordRules` (line 175) would override it to hash the content without `created_at`.
- **Old digests:** `JsonItemRules.matches_stored` (line 155) only compares against the current content in a newer format. `RecordRules` would also return true when the stored content, with any `created_at`, matches the new digest once `created_at` is dropped. The legacy digest includes the time, so the comparison must use the stored content's own `created_at`.
- **Retry path:** `reef/storage/data.py` (`item_digest_matches`, line 515) already falls back to `matches_stored`, so I expect no change there.
- **Docstring:** `reef/storage/record_items.py:8` documents the content, so its comment may need a small update.

When control starts, it reads the evaluations queue from the beginning. For each rollout item, `read_results` calls `settle`. `settle` calls `self.dispatcher.locked_scenario(scenario)`. That call raises `UnknownScenario` when the scenario was deleted. The broad `except Exception` at line 203 then logs the error with a traceback through `logger.exception`.

The fix is to catch `UnknownScenario` in that loop and skip the evaluation without logging an error.
